To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ground-state energies of a system of two particles, without spin, without quantum statistics, and interacting through central forces, increase with the angular momentum.
the ground-state energies of systems ofN particles interacting by central forces and having no spin or statistics increase with angular momentum.
the ground-state energies ofN-particle systems without spin, without spin-statistics, and interacting by two-body central forces, are nondecreasing functions of angular momentum.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ground-state of a system of N particles, with central forces, without spin and without statistics is always higher in energy than the ground-state of N-1 particles with the same forces.
the ground-state of a system of N particles without spin, and with central forces, is a function of the angular momentum which increases with the magnitude of the angular momentum.
the ground-state of a system of many particles interacting by central forces, with or without spin, and with any statistics, increases with angular momentum, provided the system is stable.
